The ATT estimate is about 0.093. This is the propensity-score (inverse-odds) weighting estimate. Here `y` is binary (employed or not), so the effect is a difference in employment probability.

- **Method:** I fit a logistic regression of `t` on x0–x16. I then reweighted the control group by p/(1−p) to resemble the treated group, and took the difference in mean `y` between the treated and the reweighted controls.
- **Raw comparison:** The unadjusted difference is negative (0.779 treated vs 0.858 control), so the covariate adjustment changes the sign.
- **Other adjusted estimates:** Two regression-based estimates came out lower. A linear regression with the covariates gives 0.081. An outcome model fit on controls only and applied to the treated gives 0.084. All three adjusted estimates agree on a positive effect of roughly 0.08 to 0.09.

ANSWER: 0.093
